name: s92-quality-gate-sigterm-ends-check
setup_commands: export CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR='{TMPROOT}'; printf '{"tool_name":"Edit","tool_input":{"file_path":"%s"}}' '{TMPROOT}/src/x.py' | bash '{KIT_ROOT}/.claude/hooks/quality-gate.sh' >/dev/null 2>&1 & pid=$!; sleep 2; kill -TERM $pid; rc=0; wait "$pid" || rc=$?; case "$rc" in 0|143) ;; *) echo "hook exited $rc, expected 0 or 143" >&2; exit 1 ;; esac; sleep 1; left=''; for f in .hook-state/.gate-output.*; do [ -e "$f" ] && left="$left $f"; done; if pgrep -f 'kitbench-term-{TMPROOT}' >/dev/null; then pkill -f 'kitbench-term-{TMPROOT}'; echo 'check still running after SIGTERM' >&2; exit 1; fi; if [ -n "$left" ]; then echo "left behind:$left" >&2; exit 1; fi
notes: Claude Code sends SIGTERM to a hook mid-check. The hook died at once, but its check kept running and .gate-output.<pid> was left behind. A trap now ends the check's process group and removes the file; the run stays 'running', so stop re-verifies it (and the second run passes).
